content.value_statement: Medical device teams need structured regulatory plans across FDA pathways, quality systems, privacy, and cybersecurity. This skill organizes those topics into practical assessments and strategies.
actual_capabilities: Compares 510(k), PMA, and De Novo pathways for medical device planning.
Structures reviews of design controls, document controls, CAPA, and management responsibilities.
Outlines submission preparation, testing evidence, labeling, and FDA response activities.
Organizes HIPAA safeguard and protected health information risk assessments.
Reviews premarket and postmarket medical device cybersecurity expectations.
Develops inspection readiness and warning letter response frameworks.
limitations: The guidance is not legal advice or an official FDA classification decision.
The skill does not access current FDA databases, guidance updates, or submission systems.
Included scripts, references, and assets are placeholders rather than implemented regulatory tools.
Final decisions require product evidence and review by qualified regulatory, legal, privacy, and clinical professionals.

use_cases.title: Select a Regulatory Pathway
use_cases.description: Compare likely FDA pathways, evidence needs, decision points, and submission risks for a proposed medical device.

use_cases.title: Assess Quality System Gaps
use_cases.description: Review design controls, document controls, CAPA, and management practices against a structured quality system framework.

use_cases.title: Prepare for an FDA Inspection
use_cases.description: Create a readiness plan covering records, staff preparation, mock inspection activities, and corrective action priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Explain FDA Pathways
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the differences between 510(k), De Novo, and PMA for a beginner. Include typical device profiles, evidence needs, and major decision points.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the main medical device submission pathways.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Pathway Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess possible FDA pathways for [device description]. State assumptions, identify missing facts, compare options, and recommend questions for a regulatory professional.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Compliance Gap Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a gap assessment for [organization and device]. Cover design controls, CAPA, documents, management responsibilities, HIPAA safeguards, and cybersecurity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prioritize quality, privacy, and security work.

prompt_templates.title: Develop an Integrated Submission Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop an FDA submission strategy for [device]. Include pathway rationale, predicate analysis, testing, software evidence, cybersecurity, labeling, Q-Sub questions, milestones, and key risks.

output_examples.input: Compare 510(k) and De Novo options for a novel clinical monitoring application.
output_examples.output: Pathway assessment: Start by confirming intended use, risk, and comparable legally marketed devices. A suitable predicate supports 510(k); otherwise, evaluate De Novo classification and special controls.

output_examples.input: Create a focused QSR gap review for a startup approaching design verification.
output: Confirm approved design inputs and traceability to planned verification.
Review design changes, risk controls, and independent design reviews.
Check document approvals, training records, supplier controls, and CAPA procedures.
Assign owners, evidence, due dates, and effectiveness checks for each gap.

output_examples.input: Outline an FDA inspection readiness plan.
output_examples.output: Readiness plan: verify high-risk records, train designated responders, prepare document retrieval, conduct a mock inspection, resolve critical gaps, and track corrective action effectiveness.

best_practices: Provide intended use, users, operating environment, risk profile, and development stage.
Separate known facts from assumptions and request citations to current official sources.
Have qualified professionals verify pathway, legal, clinical, privacy, and quality conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat general guidance as an FDA decision or clearance guarantee.
Do not provide protected health information, confidential submissions, or unnecessary personal data.
Do not rely on placeholder files or unverified regulatory references for final decisions.

faq.question: Can this skill determine my device classification?
faq.answer: It can organize a preliminary analysis. Confirm classification and pathway decisions through current FDA sources and qualified regulatory review.

faq.question: Does it prepare a complete 510(k) submission?
faq.answer: It can outline sections, evidence, testing, labeling, and review activities. It does not create or submit a validated complete application.

faq.question: Can it assess 21 CFR 820 compliance?
faq.answer: It can structure a gap assessment across major quality system topics. Objective evidence and expert review remain necessary.

faq.question: Does it replace legal or regulatory counsel?
faq.answer: No. Use its output for planning and discussion with qualified regulatory, legal, privacy, quality, and clinical professionals.

faq.question: Can it process protected health information?
faq.answer: Do not provide protected health information. Use de-identified descriptions and follow your approved privacy and security procedures.

faq.question: Are the included tools and references complete?
faq.answer: No. The packaged script, reference, and asset files are placeholders, while several named resources are not included.
